assets.description: A felled tree growing back. For each tree type in trees, a sapling and a young tree, drawn in that type's colours. assets.description: Sticks on the forest floor: crooked branches with side twigs and pale cut ends, in four shapes. One is crooked with two twigs, one long and gently bowed with a twig near the tip, one short and forked, and one zig-zag with three small twigs. They are 0.7 to 1.0 m long. Each stick on the ground gets a shape and a turn picked from its spot, and its own slight shade. Short knots with dark broken ends stick up from the bark, and one side of the bark has a darker streak. Their bark is pale grey-tan, like weathered dead wood, so they stand out from the brown forest floor and the tree trunks. The campfire uses the first shape without knots or streaks. The lean-to builds its poles from the same segments and colour. The sled keeps the old brown bark.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The foundation: four debarked logs laid side by side over one building-grid square, resting on two cross beams with a leg under each end. Each deck log differs a little in thickness, length, and turn, and the logs and beams show darker cut ends. The legs reach down to the ground, so they grow longer on the low side of a slope. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction has one stage per log: each delivered log stays in its place and turns solid during its stage, while the legs and beams fade in during the first stage.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The log wall: a 2 m stack of debarked logs laid along one edge of a foundation square. Each delivered log is cut in two, so each build stage lays two courses. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction lays the courses from the bottom up: each delivered log's two courses stay in their places and turn solid during its stage. A finished wall between the camera and the player fades out.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The door frame: two debarked-log posts on one edge of a foundation square, with a lintel across the top, 2 m tall. The doorway stays open. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction puts up the left post, the right post, then the lintel: each stays in its place and turns solid during its stage. A finished frame between the camera and the player fades out.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The roof frame: the timber skeleton of one foundation square, between the walls and the roof. Hewn beams, debarked logs squared with an adze, with chamfered corners, shallow adze marks, and pale cut ends, lie level on the top of every wall and door frame on the square's edges. Their square shape sets them apart from the round wall logs. The beams on the lower walls, which run along z, are hewn taller, so every beam top is level. A beam reaches about 0.15 m past the walls where no frame carries on beyond its end, so it stays under the steep eaves. The beams are a shade darker than the wall logs, so they read as their own part. Three hewn rafters, a little narrower than they are tall, rest on the beams and slope 35 degrees the way the frame faces, so the planks lie flat on them. Both ends of a rafter are cut upright. Where the front of a frame is an eave, the rafters reach on past the wall, under the roof's overhang. Where two frames slope away from each other, their rafters meet in pairs at the ridge, each pair held by wooden pegs, over a hewn ridge pole that runs under the planks and reaches past the gable ends under the overhang. The frame sloping down to +z or +x lays the ridge pole, with its last rafter. Where a slope rises above the beams, as at each end of a ridge, the high side of a shed roof, or the step beside a lower roof, plank gable ends (the gable-end draft) close the gap up to the roof. The frame's cost pays for them. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction has one stage per log: the beams along x, the beams along z, then the rafters one by one, with the gable ends going up with the last rafter. Each part stays in its place and turns solid during its stage. It hides with the roof above the player.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The cabin roof section: planks laid on the roof frame of one foundation square, the same planks the sawhorse cuts. It slopes 35 degrees the way its frame does, and sections one behind another share one continuous slope. Two rows that slope away from each other meet at a ridge, where the planks of the slope down to +z or +x reach a little past it, over the other slope. Grey, weathered planks lie in 6 overlapping rows across the slope, from the eaves up. Each row is short planks side by side, running down the slope, with ragged, staggered lower ends that are a little darker. Each plank lies a little less steep than the roof, so its lower end lifts over the row below and every row casts a clear shadow line. Where an edge has no section beside it, the planks reach 0.5 m past the outside of the wall, over the eaves, the gable ends, and the high side of a shed roof. As a blueprint it shows see-through, and construction lays one row of planks per stage. The roof above the player hides when they stand under it. Its valley pieces are the separate asset roof-corners, and its gable ends the draft asset gable-end.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The valley pieces of the cabin roof and its frame. No roof has a hip. Where a frame's downhill neighbour slopes at right angles to it, one wing ends against another, and the frame becomes a valley, where the two slopes meet in a gutter. At the corner of an L-shaped or U-shaped cabin, the corner frames' own turns decide which wing runs through: the wing that slopes the same way as them. The player changes this by turning the corner frames with R. Where the butted wing is deeper, its slope starts higher and runs over the corner square as a straight section, and its ridge stands above the through-roof's. The frame has a debarked-log rafter along each low edge and one corner to corner under the line where the slopes meet. Two dark, water-stained valley boards line the gutter, one on each slope, so they make a shallow V along the meeting line. They run from the square's high corner to its low corner and on under the eaves. Six rows of weathered planks, made like the straight section's, are laid on both slopes from the eaves up. Each slope's planks stop a hand's width short of the meeting line, cut a little ragged, and lap over the outer edge of their board, so the boards show between the slopes as a gutter. Construction stages match the straight frame's and roof's. The valley boards are laid with the first row of planks.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The log gable ends of the cabin roof. They close the gap between what is under an edge of a roof section and its planks: the triangle between the wall top and the roof at each end of a ridge or a shed roof, and the step where a taller wing's roof stands above a lower one. Each is a stack of debarked logs laid along the edge, like the log wall below it, standing on the frame's beam or the lower roof. Each course is a little shorter than the one below, and the roof's slope cuts its ends and top, so the gable end meets the roof with no gap. Where two gable ends meet at a corner, their logs reach past it and take turns, like the log walls' corners. They appear on their own, and go up with the last rafter of the roof frame, whose cost pays for them. The player never builds one alone.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The player debarking a log on the ground with a drawknife: the player stands just off the nearer end of the log, facing along it. A person stripping bark bends over the log with knees bent and hips back, holds the drawknife by both handles, sets the blade into the bark at the far side, and pulls it back towards the knees, rocking back with the hips. Then they lift the blade clear and reach out for the next stroke. The feet stay planted and the axe goes on the back. It is posed in code over the idle clip, and reads apart from the chop's side swing, the split's overhead drop, and the build's squat and press.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The player sawing a debarked log into planks at the sawhorse. While the player cuts planks, the log they cut is drawn lying along the top of the sawhorse beam. Game logic keeps it in its spot on the ground, and it is drawn back there if the player stops partway. A log taken from a sled parked beside the sawhorse stays drawn on the sled, so the player saws over the bare beam. The player steps up beside the beam, 0.7 m from it on the side they came from, and faces it, with the feet planted. The left hand rests on the log to hold it still. The right hand holds the bow saw, the draft saw-model, and pushes it away and pulls it back across the log in long, even strokes, one a second. The log sits at chin height, so the player stands nearly upright with the hips set back and the chin lifted a little, which keeps the big head clear of the log. The short arms reach the near edge of the log, and the stroke stays close to the body. The shoulders rock slightly with each push. The blade sinks from the top of the log at the start of the cut to its underside at the end. The axe goes on the back, and the saw shows in the hand only while sawing. The player steps up and lifts the hands over 0.45 seconds, and steps back the same way when sawing stops. It is posed in code over the idle clip, and reads apart from the chop's side swing and the debark's pull along the log. Crafting by hand, such as crafting the saw, uses the draft hand-craft-animation instead.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The bow saw the player holds while sawing planks: a thin steel blade with big teeth along its lower edge, 0.55 m long, strung across the ends of a stick bent into a bow that rises 0.2 m over it, and lashed on with turns of twine at each end. The stick tapers from its thick end at the grip and bends a little unevenly, like a cut sapling. A dark iron pin holds each end of the blade, and the teeth are set alternately left and right. It matches the saw in the approved crafting-icons. The player holds it by the near end of the bow, 1.3 times true size, like the other tools in the hand, because the player's head and beard are big for the body.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The player going to sleep on a laid bedroll or in a bed, and waking. A person going to bed sits down, lies back on their side with the head at the head end, then rolls onto their back and sleeps there, the chest rising and falling in slow breaths. The view dims to black while the night passes, and lights up on the morning. Then the person rolls onto their side again, sits up, gets their feet under them, and stands. The body plays KayKit's Lie_Down and Lie_Idle clips, blends over 0.7 s into Death_A_Pose as the back-lying pose, blends back, and plays Lie_StandUp; the lie-down and stand-up clips play a little faster than made. Code times the step onto the bedroll, the rolls, the breathing, the dimming, and the sky change. Game logic waits while it plays. It reads apart from the build's squat: the whole body goes down flat.
assets.source: KayKit Character Pack: Adventurers 1.0 by Kay Lousberg, https://kaylousberg.itch.io/kaykit-adventurers (also https://github.com/KayKit-Game-Assets/KayKit-Character-Pack-Adventures-1.0). Characters/gltf/Barbarian.glb, unchanged. Clips Lie_Down, Lie_Idle, Death_A_Pose, and Lie_StandUp

assets.description: The player reaching to pick something up or put it down. The player faces the thing, then bends at the hips and knees to the ground, or reaches out at waist height to a woodpile, chest, or sled, and straightens again. The whole motion takes 0.9 seconds. The hand gets to the thing 0.4 seconds in, which is when game logic hands it over. The low reach plays KayKit's PickUp clip and the waist-height reach its Interact clip, both from the approved player file, public/assets/player/barbarian.glb. Code stretches each clip so a wrist is lowest, or furthest forward, at the 0.4-second mark. On top of the clip, code bends the player deeper at the hips and steers that hand to the thing, up to 0.5 m ahead on the ground or 0.55 m ahead at waist height. The player blends into the reach over 0.15 seconds and out of it over 0.25 seconds, so there is no jump at either end, or when one reach cuts into the next. The axe goes on the back while the hands reach. It reads apart from the build's repeated squat and press: it is one quick dip and rise.
assets.source: Timed in code in this project. Clips PickUp and Interact from KayKit Character Pack: Adventurers 1.0 by Kay Lousberg, https://kaylousberg.itch.io/kaykit-adventurers, Characters/gltf/Barbarian.glb, unchanged

assets.description: The HUD: smoked walnut glass boxes, variant C of .scratch/hud-restyle/mockups.html, with warm text, amber accents, and line icons, in the hotbar and wheel layout. Every box, menu, and save-slot card is dark walnut glass that blurs the scene behind it, with a faint light edge, round corners, and a soft shadow. Without blur support, the glass is nearly opaque. The clock is a pill whose sun or moon icon sits in an amber ring that fills as the day passes, followed by the time of day as a word, such as "morning". The pause button is round. Banners are pills led by a glowing amber dot. Menus have a small-capitals heading, and the pointed row gets an amber tint. The backpack is a hotbar at the bottom centre. It opens with the backpack icon inside a ring that fills with the backpack's weight as a share of its limit, then a thin divider. The ring and icon are amber. At 90% of the limit or more, they turn to the warning colour and the icon pulses. Pointing at or focusing the ring shows the exact weight in a pill label, such as "5.5 of 20 kg". Each hotbar cell is a 58 px square with a 12 px radius and a faint light fill, holding a 38 px icon, its number key bottom left at half opacity, and its count top right. A cell shows its name only while the player points at it or focuses it, in a pill label above it, with what its contents weigh, such as "Plank ×5 · 10 kg", and the cell gets an amber outline. The build and craft buttons sit side by side at the right end of the hotbar, apart from the backpack contents. Each is a 58 px square with an amber tint, its icon over its name, and its key in the top right corner. The needs sit in a glass group to the left of the hotbar, bottom aligned with it. Each need is a 42 px ring in its own colour that fills with the need's level, with its icon inside and its name below in 10 px text. A low need pulses. On a screen too narrow for both side by side, the need group moves above the hotbar. The panels and open chest sit above them. The open chest or shelf shows its weight with a smaller ring of the same kind in its heading. While placing, the hint names its keys, such as "R to rotate · Esc to cancel". The clock is top left and the pause button top right. Build and craft open as lists above their buttons. A build row shows the structure's icon, name, and cost. A craft row shows the result's icon, the recipe name, its cost and time, and what it lacks.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The chest: a rough box hewn from debarked logs, 0.9 m wide and 0.55 m deep. Its body has a square post at each corner, three stacked planks in each wall with thin gaps between them, and a wooden grip on each end. Its lid is three planks laid side by side with a small overhang, held by two battens across the top. Each plank is a slightly different shade, and cut ends show pale. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction builds the body in the first stage and puts on the lid in the second.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The shelf: a rustic frame of pale sawn planks, 0.9 m wide, 0.4 m deep, and 1.2 m tall. Four square corner posts stand on the ground as short feet and hold two shelf boards and a top that overhangs a little. Each board rests on a rail at each side, has a lip under its front edge, and is pegged to the front posts with dark pegs. Three planks stand side by side as the back, with a slanted brace across them. Each plank is a slightly different shade. It does not show what it holds. As a blueprint it shows see-through, the stages whose planks it has wait pale and half solid, and construction builds it in three stages: the posts with the lowest board, the middle board and the top, then the back.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: Build menu icons for furniture built from planks, drawn in the build icons' shaded style on the same 24 by 24 grid. Each icon is drawn from its furniture's model, seen from the front and a little above, as the chest's build icon is. The shelf: three dark back planks, two shelf boards, an overhanging top, two front posts that stand on the ground as feet, and a dark peg where each board meets a post. The bed: seen from the foot end, a headboard of two planks, a linen mattress inside the frame, a pillow, a blue blanket over the foot half, a footboard of two planks, and two legs. The table: seen from its long side, a top of four planks, the rail under it, two front legs, and two back legs in shadow. The stool: a low square seat of two boards, four straight legs, the rail between the front legs, and a lower rail along each side. Furniture ticket 03 added the shelf icon, ticket 02 (.scratch/furniture/issues/02-bed.md) added the bed icon, ticket 04 (.scratch/furniture/issues/04-table.md) the table icon, and ticket 05 (.scratch/furniture/issues/05-stool-and-sitting.md) the stool icon.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The sawhorse: a beam of debarked log, 1.2 m long, resting 0.75 m up in the crook of two pairs of crossed legs, one pair near each end. The legs spread 0.6 m at the foot. Every part is painted like the debarked log, with drawknife streaks, bark scraps near the ends, knots, and darker heartwood on the cut ends. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its place, and construction stands up the legs in the first stage and lays the beam in the second.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The sled: two log runners made from the logs asset's Kenney log, stretched to 1.8 m and lying side by side 0.8 m apart, with four crooked sticks laid across them. The front of each runner curves up and narrows like a skid. Dark rope lashes each stick to each runner in an X, and a tow rope runs in a V from the runner tips to a loop in front. While the player drags the sled, this flat tow rope hides and the draft sled-rope draws it lifted instead. The runners show dark bark and pale cut ends, and the sticks are the stick colour with pale cut ends. As a blueprint it shows see-through, each delivered log waits pale and half solid in its runner's place, and construction lays one runner per log, then one lashed cross piece per stick; the last brings the tow rope. A finished sled shows the 0 to 6 logs and debarked logs on it, lying along the runners: logs first, then debarked logs, stacked in a pyramid of three on the cross pieces, two above, and one on top. They use the logs and debarked-log shapes. A sled the player has dragged points the way it was last pulled, front first, at any angle.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The 0 to 24 planks lying on a finished sled, drawn on top of the approved sled model. Each plank is the pile's plank shape: a flat board of pale sawn wood, 0.8 m long, in one of three near tones, with darker sawn ends. The planks lie flat along the runners in layers of eight, two end to end and four side by side. Each layer and plank slides a little so the ends of the stack are ragged. Two rope lashings bind every full layer. Planks in a layer that is not full lie loose on top. They rest on the cross pieces when the sled holds no logs, and on top of the logs when it does.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The action queue beside the clock, and the icons for queued actions on things that have no icon elsewhere. The row is a smoked walnut glass pill right of the clock pill, holding one round chip per queued action, up to 4. The action under way comes first, in a larger chip with a faint amber ring. Pointing at a chip tints it amber and shows the action's name in a pill label below it, as a hotbar cell does. With an empty queue, the row is gone. Each chip shows what its action works on. Backpack contents, structures, furniture, the sled, logs, and debarked logs reuse their approved icons. Three icons, drawn in the build icons' shaded style on the same 24 by 24 grid, cover the rest: a standing tree, a conifer of three green tiers on a short brown trunk, standing on a grassy patch; the river, a blue stream with pale ripples winding across a round grassy patch; and a spot on the ground to walk to, an amber pin on a patch of earth. The tree and the pin share one ground patch, each with a soft shadow.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: Icons drawn in the build icons' shaded style: the sled, seen from the front left and a little above, with two log runners whose front tips curl up like skids, the far runner darker and higher up, four crooked sticks lashed across them with dark rope Xs, and a pale tow rope running in a V from the tips to a loop in front. It shows on the sled's build menu tile and on the hotbar's sled cell while the player drags a sled. The log, a log on its side with dark bark and a pale cut end, shows in the sled's cost.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: A woodpile: two rails of debarked log on the ground, held in by two stakes at each end, with logs, debarked logs, and firewood stacked across them, four to a layer, from empty to full at five layers. Logs, debarked logs, and firewood use their approved shapes. Each layer rests in the gaps of the one below. As a blueprint, the rails and stakes show see-through.
assets.source: Built in code in this project
approvalNotes: 2026-11-11: The owner approved the stacked version: approved log, debarked log, and firewood shapes, layers nested in the gaps, debarked rails, and four stakes.

assets.description: How each kind of dropped thing looks on the ground, from one to many. A pile shows one copy of its kind for each thing it holds, up to 12. Firewood lies in a stack of 5, 4, then 3, each layer resting in the gaps of the one below. Bark lies in up to three rows of strips, each strip nested in the one below. Tools, food, the pot, and the bedroll spread around the middle. Firewood, bark, mushrooms, and the pot reuse their approved shapes. The axe has a steel head and a handle painted red at its end, the knife a bright blade, the drawknife a blue-steel blade with two wooden handles, and the steel and flint is the "steel-and-flint" asset. A handful of berries is seven red berries on a leaf. Dropped sticks never form a pile: they lie as normal sticks. The saw blade, the saw, and the plank are rough draft shapes added by the crafting feature.
assets.source: Built in code in this project
approvalNotes: 2026-11-11: The owner approved keeping rough draft shapes for the saw blade, the saw, and the plank in the pile until they are polished.

assets.description: How the fishing line, the fishing rod, raw fish, and cooked fish look lying in a pile, laid out like the other things in the approved pile. The fishing line is a flat wooden winder, 10 cm long with a crossbar at each end, and pale line wound round its middle, with a small wire hook caught in the line. The fishing rod is a thin wooden rod, 1.5 m long and thicker at the butt, with a 25 cm cord-wrapped grip, spare line wound just above the grip, and 30 cm of pale line trailing from its tip to a hook. A raw fish is a 30 cm trout lying on its side: a body that tapers from a blunt head to a forked tail, a fin on its back and a smaller one under its tail, a grey-green back, a pale belly along its lower side, and a dark eye. A cooked fish is the same trout with browned skin, a golden belly, and three dark char marks across its upper side. The fishing animation hangs the same raw fish from the line, and the campfire uses it too.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The fishing rod in the player's hands while they fish, matching the rod in fishing-piles: a thin wooden rod, 1.5 m long, made of two sticks joined end to end. It tapers from the butt to the tip and bows gently down towards the tip. A dark cord grip wraps the butt where the right hand holds it, with spare pale line wound just above. Dark cord lashes the sticks where they meet, two trimmed twig knots stand on the lower stick, and a knot of pale line is tied at the tip. The player holds it at true size. The line runs from the tip and is drawn with the fishing animation.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: Up to 3 fish cooking on a campfire, spread round the stone ring. Each fish is the trout from fishing-piles, skewered lengthwise and snout up on a pale peeled stick 80 cm long, whose pointed tip pokes out past the snout. The stick is pushed into the ground just outside the stones and leans in a little, so the fish hangs above the stones with its flat side to the flames, well below the pot nested on the fire's sticks. As a fish cooks, its grey-green back darkens to brown, its pale belly turns golden, and dark char marks show on both its flat sides. A fish keeps its colour while the fire is out.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The player fishing from the river bank with a fixed line on a pole, facing the spot on the river they clicked. The rod has no reel, so the player fishes the way people fish with a cane pole: they flick the rod back past the right shoulder, pause while the line straightens behind, then drive it forward and stop it sharply so the line rolls out in an arc and lands on the water. The right hand holds the butt and the left hand grips a little further up. The weight rocks back on the back cast and forward on the forward cast. The rod tip lags behind the swing and springs past at the stop. While they wait, the rod is held out at chest height with its tip bobbing gently, and the slack line sags to a small cork float with a painted top and a quill. When a fish bites, the float bobs and goes under and the rod tip jerks down. The player snaps the rod up to set the hook, the rod bends hard, and the line goes taut. They lift the rod high, the raw fish comes up out of the water hanging head up from the hook, thrashing, and swings in on the line. The left hand lets go of the rod and catches it, 1.6 seconds after the bite. The next cast starts from there, as the fish goes in the backpack. The cast takes 1.4 seconds. The axe goes on the back, and the rod shows in the hands only while fishing. The player lifts the rod from standing over 0.35 seconds, and lowers it the same way when fishing stops. It is posed in code over the idle clip.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The bedroll lying rolled up on the ground after the player drops it: the laid bedroll rolled up, green canvas outside with the red blanket spiralling through each end, a hemmed loose flap, and two leather straps with brass buckles.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The fire-lighting kit, called steel and flint in the game. On the ground it is a C-shaped steel of dark blued steel, a straight striking bar with each end curled back into a loop, with a dark grey shard of flint lying behind it, about 11 cm wide in all. Its backpack icon shows the C-steel, the flint above it, and orange sparks flying off the flint.
assets.source: Built in code in this project
approvalNotes: 2026-11-12: The owner asked in chat to change the fire striker to a kit of steel and flint, with its own entry, a redrawn backpack icon, and the name Steel and flint. The owner approved the C-steel and flint shard and asked to call it steel and flint everywhere.

assets.description: The bed: a cabin bed 1 m wide and 2 m long. Four square corner posts with capped tops stand tall at the head and low at the foot, joined by rails, with seven slats across them. The headboard is five upright planks under a top rail, the footboard four. Each plank is a slightly different shade of pale sawn wood. On the slats lies a pale linen mattress with a soft top edge and a plump pillow, and a blue wool blanket covers the foot half, hanging down over the side rails, with its top edge turned back. As a blueprint it shows see-through, the stages whose planks it has wait pale and half solid, and construction builds it in four stages: the frame, the slats, the head and foot boards, then the bedding. To sleep, the player steps up onto the mattress, turned to lie along the bed, plays the approved sleep animation there, and steps back down beside the bed once standing.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The table: a top 1.2 m long, 0.8 m deep, and 0.75 m high, in the style of a farmhouse table. The top is four planks laid along its length with thin gaps between them, held between two cleats across its ends, with a dark peg through each cleat into each plank. The top overhangs a frame of four rails, with a dark peg where each long rail meets a leg. Four thick square legs stand under the frame, joined near the ground by an H-shaped stretcher. Each plank is a slightly different shade of pale sawn wood. As a blueprint, the table shows see-through. Stages whose planks it already has show pale and half solid. Construction builds it in three stages: the legs with the stretcher, the rails, then the top.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The stool: a small square seat of two pale sawn boards, 0.4 m across and 0.27 m high, on four square legs. The seat overhangs the legs a little, two battens under it hold the boards together, and dark pegs on top mark where the legs join it. Rails join the legs low on the left and right and higher at the front and back. Each plank is a slightly different shade. As a blueprint it shows see-through, a stage whose plank it has waits pale and half solid, and construction builds it in two stages: the legs with their rails, then the seat.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The player sitting on a stool, resting, and standing up. The player steps up to the stool over 0.5 seconds, turning their back to it to face the way it faces, and sits down. They rest there, breathing, for as long as they sit. When they walk or act, they stand up and step back to where they stood. If they stand while still sitting down, they rise along the same path. The seated body rests on the seat, and the short legs hang just above the ground. The body plays KayKit's Sit_Chair_Down, Sit_Chair_Idle, and Sit_Chair_StandUp clips from the approved player file, public/assets/player/barbarian.glb; code times the step to the stool and back. The axe goes on the back while the player sits.
assets.source: Timed in code in this project. Clips Sit_Chair_Down, Sit_Chair_Idle, and Sit_Chair_StandUp from KayKit Character Pack: Adventurers 1.0 by Kay Lousberg, https://kaylousberg.itch.io/kaykit-adventurers, Characters/gltf/Barbarian.glb, unchanged
assets.license: Project code. The clips are CC0 1.0

assets.description: The player lashes a small bundle of sticks by hand, for a hand recipe such as the saw or the fishing rod. Real lashing: one hand holds the work and turns it, the other passes the cord over, under and back round, then pulls it tight with a short, sharp tug. The player stands still, rounds the shoulders, and bows the head to watch. The left hand holds a bundle of two pale sticks at waist height, in front of the belly, with a dark brown binding and a cord running to the right hand. Each 2-second cycle: the right hand winds once round the bundle while the left hand rolls it forward to meet the cord, holds on top, tugs the cord out to the side as the shoulders dip, bounces as the cord snaps tight, then settles back on top. The axe goes on the back. The hands lift to the work over 0.25 seconds when crafting starts. When it stops, the player stands straight back up at once, the bundle disappears, and the axe returns to the hand. It is posed in code over the idle clip. Cutting planks at the sawhorse uses sawing-animation instead.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The player dragging a sled. A real hauler pulling a loaded sled by a short rope holds it in one hand behind them, arm straight back, and leans forward so body weight does the pulling, heaving a little further into the rope at each push-off. Here the left hand holds the rope low behind the left hip, so the right hand stays free to swing the axe or steady a log on the right shoulder. The body leans forward from the hips with the chin up. Each step of the walk heaves the chest further over and pulls the rope hand back, then eases off as the other foot lands. The legs keep the walk's stride, played at the slower dragging pace so the feet stay planted. Standing still while dragging shows the same lean over the idle clip, with no heave. The lean starts and ends at once with dragging. It is posed in code over the approved walk-animation or the idle clip, with the build pose's bones. The rope is the draft sled-rope.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The short rope the player drags a sled by. While the sled is dragged it takes the place of the sled's own tow rope. It runs in a V from the two runner tips to a knot 34 cm in front of them, lifted toward the hand, and from the knot to the player's left hand, held low behind the left hip. A turn of rope wraps the hand, and an 11 cm tail hangs from it. It is light hemp, laid from three twisted strands, 2.2 cm across, the same colour as the parked sled's tow rope. While the player walks it pulls taut and sags 2 cm. When they stand still it goes slack: it sags 15 cm, the knot drops 8 cm, and the V sags 3 cm. It eases between the two in about 0.15 s. It follows the player and the sled as they move, shows only while the player drags a sled, and hides at once when they let go.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: Short motions the player plays once, each about one second. Foraging a berry bush leans in from the hips, pushes the right hand into the middle of the bush, plucks with a quick tug back, and drops the berries into the left hand, cupped in front of the belly. Eating raises the right hand to the mouth and bites twice: the head ducks in to bite and pulls back to tear, then nods while chewing. Drinking from the river kneels at the river bank, scoops water toward the body with both hands cupped, and raises them to the mouth with the head tipped back. Filling the pot kneels at the river bank and dips the approved pot into the water, which fills as the hand gets there. Drinking from the pot raises it to the mouth and tips it back, with two gulps. The player faces the bush or the river. A bite or drink taken while walking or working plays over the walk or the work, moving only the arms and head. Walking or another action that starts after a motion began cuts it short. Posed in code on top of the idle clip; the axe goes on the back. Foraging mushrooms reuses the approved pick-up-animation.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: Stone: how it looks lying on the ground in a pile, and its backpack icon. In a pile, each stone is a low, lumpy, grey river stone about 20 cm long with flat faces, spread around the middle like other things in a pile. The backpack icon, drawn in the same style as backpack-icons, is two rounded grey river stones, a big one in front of a smaller one, with a glint on the big one. The same stone shape shows in the player's hands while gathering stone.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The player gathers one stone at the water's edge: they crouch, reach both hands low in front, feel about for a stone, then rise halfway and lift it to the chest in both hands. One lift takes 4 seconds, as long as gathering one stone. The player faces the spot clicked. Posed in code on top of the idle clip; the axe goes on the back.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The fireplace: a squat stone hearth on one foundation square, about 1.7 m tall. A back wall and two side walls of grey river stone, two courses high, stand round a stone hearth floor, with the opening at the front. A stone slab lies across their tops, and a short chimney of two stone blocks under a cap rises from the back. The stones are plain boxes in three greys. As a blueprint it shows see-through, the stones it already has wait pale and half solid, and construction lays one stone per stage, 12 in all: the hearth floor, the walls, the slab, then the chimney. Each stone fades in above its place and is set down. A lit fireplace shows the approved fire-effect on its hearth floor, shrunk to 55%, with the campfire's glow and pool of light hung at its opening. A pot on its fire shows the approved pot sitting on the flames under the slab, steaming while lit. Fish on its fire show the approved fish-on-fire skewers standing upright in a row of 3 just in front of the opening, with their flat sides to the fire.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The build menu icon for the fireplace, drawn in the build icons' shaded style on the same 24 by 24 grid: a squat grey stone hearth seen from the front, with cut lines between the stones, a pale stone mantel across its top, a sooty arched opening with a small orange flame in it, and a short darker chimney rising behind.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The torch: a brown stick about 55 cm long with a head of bark wrapped round its top end, tied with two dark bands, its tip charred black. Lit, it rides upright in the player's left hand, leaning a little forward and out, through walking, work, carrying a log, and dragging a sled. A small copy of the approved fire-effect, about a sixth of a campfire's size, burns on its head. A warm orange point light at the flame flickers and lights the ground about 6 m around the player. It casts no shadows. Unlit torches lie on their sides in a pile, spread like other things in a pile. Planted, the lit torch stands upright with its butt a little in the ground or the foundation deck, with the same small flame and a soft orange glow round it that lights nothing. Four warm orange point lights stay in the scene at all times, at zero strength while unused. Each frame they go to the torch in the hand first, then to the planted torches nearest the camera. Planted torches added by torch ticket 02 (.scratch/torch/issues/02-plant-a-torch.md).
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: The torch icons, drawn in the backpack icons' shaded style on the same 24 by 24 grid. The unlit torch, the backpack icon and the craft menu icon, is a brown stick leaning right with a head of bark tied round its top, its tip charred dark. The lit torch, shown in the hotbar cell for the torch in the player's hand, is the same torch with an orange flame and a yellow heart rising from the head. That cell sits apart from the backpack cells, like the shoulder cell, with a thin amber gauge along its bottom that shrinks as the torch burns down. Its label says how long the torch still burns, such as "Lit torch · 2 h 10 min left".
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: A plank door hung in a door frame. Three upright planks of pale sawn wood, each a little lighter or darker than the next, fill the doorway between the frame's posts, about 0.48 m wide and 1.76 m tall, with a thin gap to the posts and the lintel. Two darker battens run across the inside face, and a small dark iron latch sits on the outside, on the side away from the hinges at the left post. As a blueprint it shows see-through, planks it already has wait pale and half solid, and construction lays one plank per stage, 3 in all; the battens and latch go on with the last plank. Each plank fades in above its place and is set down. It shows shut, open, or part way, as door-animation turns it, and fades with its frame when it stands between the camera and the player.
assets.source: Built in code in this project

assets.description: A door swinging open and shut on its hinges at the left post. When the player comes within 1 m of the middle of the door frame, the door swings open, away from the side the player stands on, to 100 degrees from shut. Once the player is more than 1 m away, it swings back shut. A full swing takes 0.45 seconds, easing in and out. A door that turns back part way through a swing returns at the same pace, so it takes less time.
assets.source: Timed in code in this project

assets.description: The build menu icons for the floor and the door, drawn in the build icons' shaded style on the same 24 by 24 grid. The door icon is a door of three upright pale wooden planks, seen from the front, hung in a pale log door frame with a lintel across the top. Two darker battens cross the planks, and a small dark latch sits on the right.
assets.source: Built in code in this project
